grades.quote: sleep acquires p->lock (2714) and _only then_ releases the condition lock lk. The fact that sleep holds one or the other of these locks at all times is what prevents a concurrent wakeup (which must acquire and hold both) from acting, and thus prevents a lost wake-up.
grades.reason: Explains the lost-wakeup race and the locking sequence needed to prevent it.

grades.quote: A thread that finds circumstances not to its liking executes the wait operation and thereby goes to sleep until such time as another thread invokes the notify operation.
grades.reason: Provides background on waiting and notification, but does not explain lost wakeups or the check-to-sleep race.

grades.quote: It holds wait_lock because it’s the condition lock for the wakeup(p->parent), preventing a parent in wait from losing the wakeup.
grades.reason: Gives a useful concrete example of preventing missed wakeups with a condition lock, without fully explaining the general race.

grades.quote: A call to wakeup at that point would find no sleeping process to wake up; the wakeup would simply return. But then the call to sleep might never wake up, since the wakeup intended for it has already happened.
grades.reason: Directly diagnoses the reported symptom as a lost wakeup and explains the condition-lock and atomic-sleep remedy.
